problem_statement:
Stride Range is a running-shoe store built on the uakp98/shoe_store RedStore commerce template (repo_id uakp98__shoe_store__30f34c38ec75) with pages home, products, product detail, cart and account. It needs a working Fit Lab finder that lets shoppers browse the store's sizing, fit and care guides in-context and carry that finder across the shopping surfaces. Build a native interactive guide finder on the Fit Lab page and register it on the product-browsing pages so the experience is continuous.

(1) On fit-lab.html render a Fit Lab finder: a category tab row (All guides / Sizing / Fit / Care) above a grid of six guide cards (two per category), each card built from an existing product image plus a title, a category label and grounded copy. A live readout below the tabs must read "Showing 6 of 6 · All guides" on load.
(2) Clicking a category tab must filter the grid to that category AND update the readout to "Showing N of 6 · <Category>" (e.g. clicking Fit shows the two Fit cards and reads "Showing 2 of 6 · Fit"). The clicked tab becomes the active tab.
(3) The same finder bar must also appear on products.html and products-details.html so the guide finder is continuous across the product-browsing flow, using the store's existing containers, orange accent and rounded white cards.
(4) The tab row and the card grid must stay inside the viewport on mobile (390px) with no horizontal overflow, and the active tab plus the card copy must remain legible.
required_content: A Fit Lab finder on fit-lab.html with tabs All guides / Sizing / Fit / Care and six guide cards.
A live readout that reads 'Showing 6 of 6 · All guides' before any tab is clicked.
Clicking the Fit tab filters to two cards and updates the readout to 'Showing 2 of 6 · Fit'.
The Fit Lab finder bar is also present on products.html and products-details.html.
No horizontal overflow on mobile; the active tab and card copy stay legible.
design_constraints: Reuse the Stride Range containers (.small-container, .row), the orange #ff523b accent color, the rounded 22px pill tabs, and the white product cards with a 12px border-radius and a soft box-shadow.

The responsive tab-row layout must wrap on narrow viewports (display:flex, flex-wrap:wrap, min-width:0 on the tabs) so it never overflows the 390px mobile viewport; the card grid layout stacks to a single full-width column on mobile.

The active tab button must keep an accessible contrast ratio (white text on the #ff523b orange fill), and the guide-card typography — titles, category labels and body copy — must remain dark gray (#555) on a white background.

Each guide card keeps the store's white card style with a 12px border-radius, a light pink #ffd6d6 border and a soft shadow, with consistent 18px padding and spacing between the image, title and copy; the desktop grid layout is a three-column wrapping flex with a 20px gap.
The Fit Lab finder must not overlap or shingle its cards; each card occupies its own row/column position with normal (non-negative) margins so the six guide cards are all fully visible and legible.
state_constraints: desktop_fitlab shows all six guide cards and the readout 'Showing 6 of 6 · All guides'.
desktop_fitlab_fit is desktop_fitlab after clicking the Fit tab: two cards, readout 'Showing 2 of 6 · Fit'.
desktop_products and desktop_product_detail both include the Fit Lab finder bar.

change_completion: The Fit Lab finder renders on fit-lab.html with the tab row, six guide cards and the live readout.
Clicking the Fit tab filters the grid to two cards and the readout reads 'Showing 2 of 6 · Fit'.
design_consistency: The finder reuses the Stride Range containers, orange accent, rounded pills and white cards.
The finder bar appears consistently on fit-lab.html, products.html and products-details.html.
interaction_continuity: The tab click updates both the active-tab styling and the count readout without a reload.
The pre-click readout reads 'Showing 6 of 6 · All guides' and the post-click readout reflects the chosen category.
regression: The existing home, products, product-detail, cart and account pages must preserve their original RedStore/Stride Range layout, product grid, hero and footer without any content removed, restyled or reflowed.

Adding the Fit Lab finder must not regress the untouched pages: their headings, product cards, navigation and copy stay byte-identical, no forbidden RedStore placeholder text appears, and there are zero console errors across all states.
responsive: The tab row wraps and the card grid stacks to a single column on the 390px mobile viewport with no horizontal overflow.
The Fit Lab finder is legible on desktop, tablet and mobile viewports.

author_notes: Native lever: the store's own Fit Lab finder — a category tab filter over six guide cards with a live 'Showing N of 6 · Category' count. This is a genre-native commerce guide finder, not a bolted-on metric rail; it sits in the Stride Range product-browsing flow. The finder is the D3 visual host AND the D4 interaction control. Assets used: images/product-11.jpg, product-3.jpg, product-5.jpg, product-2.jpg, product-7.jpg, product-10.jpg, plus images/logo.png and the footer app-badge images (play-store.png / app-store.png). Reference: correct finder (filters + live count), fluid wrapping tab row, legible white cards. Baseline: the finder wiring is correct (so it passes the interaction check) but its tab row is a fixed 760px nowrap strip that overflows the mobile viewport, and the finder is only present on fit-lab.html — it is missing from products.html and products-details.html. Bad: a smart-but-broken finder — the tab row overflows on mobile, the active tab is near-white text on a near-white pill and the six guide cards shingle over one another with cascading negative margins and near-white illegible copy (a collapsed, illegible lever region); the finder JS snapshots the guide list and readout at init so clicking a tab toggles the active pill but never re-filters the grid or updates the count (stale 'Showing 6 of 6 · All guides'); and the finder is missing from products-details.html.

metadata.selected_repo_reason: The static RedStore shoe template already has a home page, products grid, product detail, cart, account, local product imagery, footer app badges and a responsive mobile menu, but lacks an interactive guide finder that carries across the product-browsing flow — an ideal host for a native Fit Lab category filter with a live count.
